In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure‐activity relationships for the K+ channel blockage by tetraalkyammonium ions and the binding of these ions to the KcsA potassium channel.
the development of molecular modelling techniques for the study of ligand–receptor interactions.
the development of new methods for the calculation of binding free energies of ligands to biological systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the KcsA potassium channel is a highly efficient tetraalkyl ammonium ion blocker, and that the binding of the tetraalkyl ions to the channel can be described in terms of a combination of the size of the ion and the conformation of the binding site.
the tetraalkyl ammonium ions are not the most potent blockers, as they have been thought to be, but that the tetraethyl ammonium ion is the best blocker among them.
the binding of a tetraalkylmonium ion to a potassium channel is a complex process involving several steps and different binding sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of molecular dynamics free energy calculations with automated ligand‐binding docking is an efficient method for the study of ligand‐protein binding, and can give a good description of the binding free energies and the structure‐activity relationships for the ligands.
the binding free energy of a tetraalkylmonium ion to the KcsA potassium channel can be predicted to an accuracy of 1.5 kcal/mol using molecular modelling.
the binding of a tetraalkyl ammonium ion is determined by the size of the alkyl chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the binding of tetraalkyl ammonium ions to KcsA is governed by a balance of enthalpic and entropic effects, with the former dominated by the interaction between the positively charged ammonium group of the ligands and the negatively charged Asp80 residues of the protein, and the latter by the loss of rotational entropy upon ligand binding to the channel.
the relative binding free energies of tetraalkyl ammonium ions to the KcsA K+ channel correlate with the relative binding free energy differences of the same ions to the K+ channel.

the binding free energy of a tetraalkyl ammonium ion to the KcsA potassium channel can be calculated with a reasonable level of accuracy, and that the binding of the tetraalkyl ions to the Kcsa potassium channel is mainly determined by electrostatic interactions.
